en: This is the spirit of your dear father,
[Meaning uncertain: opening word unresolved.]
uncertainty_note: The opening word is unresolved; its initial resembles К rather than Н. The former interpretation as a proper name Nadishin and a claim of geographical origin are not established by the handwriting. Kyrgyz retained provisionally pending a defensible full reading.

en: His first ancestor was a khan,
He used to support him from the beginning [reading uncertain],
uncertainty_note: The overwritten first word remains provisional. The following words read колдоп жүрчү эле, rather than келген жүргүзүп эле; the object is implicit.

en: Kara Kozhal was of the Arabs,
Of the hero Booruk Kenen,
He was the one appointed,
Father Kalka became khan,
[Meaning uncertain: opening words unresolved.]
uncertainty_note: Opening words remain unresolved; neither the proposed Темик nor the interpretation involving laughter is secure. Kyrgyz retained provisionally; the previous fluent English was unsupported.

en: Making a people by Heaven's will,
Making the strength of his weapons,
Making the gathered clans a people,
Though oppressed, he grew mighty,
Multiplying from solitude,
Becoming the equal of the whole world,
Arstan Kozhal, the brave warrior,
Finding no mountain to dash against [reading uncertain],
uncertainty_note: The opening is provisionally read Урунарга; the internal joins remain indistinct. The former Үрүндө and English reference to an advance were unsupported.

en: Finding no enemy to wage war against,
Those people who heeded words,
He made into a people with his speech,
The fool who would not heed words,
He bent by force to his will,
No one had dared face him,
Saying, “Valiant Kenen, conquer!”,
He spared no enemy side,
The horse he rode was a bay charger,
Where the bay charger had not trotted or walked,
No land remained intact,
That Kenen did not demand and take,
No people remained intact,
That had not tried a cunning stratagem,
None of the cunning remained intact,
That Kyrgyz Kenen had not struck,
None among the peoples remained intact,
[Meaning uncertain: pale line unresolved.]
uncertainty_note: The pale line remains unresolved. Its ending may be өткүр шер rather than отур жер, so the former English about a central land where a sultan sits is not defensible. Kyrgyz retained provisionally; no speculative replacement adopted.

en: The foremost warrior born into the world,
Eloquent in speech, a wise man,
He granted whatever was wished,
He beat back the wrathful,
He reconciled what could not be reconciled,
Whatever anyone said to me,
He supplied an answer to them all,
Dust rose as though the earth had stirred,
A murmuring host came forth,
No man dared approach him face to face,
Narrow in temper, he would not open his hand,
The radiance never left his face.
Keeping companions, he gathered brave men,
From Tölögön's people he gathered his peers,

uncertainty_note: The first word appears to be Коң; the manuscript spelling is uncommon.
en: The land sustained their great chiefs,
Gathering the multitude, he cared for the people,
His thousand warriors who laid siege,
All those who had wandered,
Filling sacks with yellow gold,
Thinking deeply, he sustained the people,
Taking on the fury of a tiger,
He came to be called Kenen the Tiger,
Making the hero's arrow ready,
The enemy who poured out his wrath,
He destroyed him and drew blood,
No people remained to speak against him,
Saying, 'The mighty Kozhal has fallen,'
From his father to his forefathers,

uncertainty_note: The first word reads Казынадай, but its final suffix is visually uncertain.
en: Like a treasure upon his head,
Saying that fortune and prosperity had settled upon him,
The people spoke throughout the great realm,
Saying he had become the father of the people,
Whenever he seemed spent, he flared up anew,
He had grown strong from his very roots.
After each one died, in pursuit,
I myself led those who would strike them down,
uncertainty_note: The final word appears to be эрчиткен; the middle word may instead be кырлар.

en: [Uncertain: will they find the cart-load, frozen?]
uncertainty_note: All four word shapes are visible, but the phrase is not securely intelligible; арбан and балы may be different lexemes.

en: His heroism is great as well.
His own eyes saw it clearly,
The foremost sage,
Racing across the face of the earth,
He would emerge alone from the race,
His four racehorses were ready,
uncertainty_note: The first two words are pale and may have a different reading; күлүгү is inferred from the racing context.

en: From Saykal, whom the prince had taken,
uncertainty_note: The middle word is difficult; it resembles алган, while the final proper name reads Сайкалдан.

en: There was a soul who followed behind me.
Settling them on two summer pastures,
Was it the multitude that migrated?
uncertainty_note: The first word is a best-effort reading of a compressed cursive form; the line may instead contain көчүшкөн.

en: I lived in freedom,
Delighting the people, he went laughing,
uncertainty_note: жүрдү күлүп is the likely reading, but several letters overlap and are faint.

en: He had become the people's enclosure and refuge,
His heroism, his lionhearted courage,
Now it struck the palate like springtime,
uncertainty_note: The first two words remain unresolved at lexical level; this is a letter-shape transcription and the English is provisional.

en: If he roared fearsomely,
uncertainty_note: The final verb resembles чаңырса, but could be a closely related formula involving чаң.

en: His eyes reddening like a lion's,
[Uncertain: his mouth like a bow ...]
uncertainty_note: Жаадай and оозун are plausible; the final word is not securely deciphered and the line cannot be translated confidently.

en: Stretching out across the open steppe,
With a hundred close companions,
uncertainty_note: The possessive ending in жолдошуң and the numeral жүз are the likeliest readings, though both are cursively compressed.

en: His comrades were brave men,
[Uncertain: seething, equal in merriment,]
uncertainty_note: The line is fully visible but its second and third lexical forms are not secure; English follows the tentative reading.

en: When a black gun cracked,
Brave Kenen, who would not flee,
When a great gun boomed,
uncertainty_note: The first word is heavily cursive and may be another adjective; мылтык тарс этсе is clear.

en: Lionhearted Kenen would not startle and flee,
His majesty mounting, his wrath sharp,
uncertainty_note: This is a contextual normalization of difficult cursive; артып and курч are not fully secure on letter shape alone.

en: Noble Kenen, the gray-maned wolf,
[Uncertain: come as a somewhat superior equal,]
uncertainty_note: The final baseline is fully visible but remains lexically unresolved; this is the closest letter-shape reading.
